body: October is too early for Bing Crosby and peppermint cocoa – but if you’re considering a beauty advent calendar, you’re right on time.
We have tested popular calendars from Anthropologie, Lush, Charlotte Tilbury and Amazon’s sold-out edition to see if any live up to the hype – and we math-ed out the true value of each.

Thus far, Revolve’s has had the best cost-to-value ratio of them all. The brand, perhaps best known for its huge catalogue of high-end, trendy clothing, doesn’t offer glitzy dresses or funnel-neck jackets in its calendar, just a ton of the best beauty products packed in a charming pink suitcase.

Its 25-day beauty advent calendar has a listed value of $953, but only costs $150. As we are always on the lookout for truly good deals, we tested it alongside its cheaper 12-day option. Below, we reviewed the de-bloating supplements, body lotions and sleep masks in each calendar. In the end, one came out on top.

articles.title: A financially comfortable friend has set up a GoFundMe for vet bills. Is this socially acceptable? | Leading questions
articles.summary: Your friends may have had good intentions when making this ask, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But that needn’t dictate how you feel about it. A friend, who I believe is financially comfortable, set up a GoFundMe page to pay for vet bills for their sick dog while on holiday overseas.
body: The family appears to be financially comfortable; both adults have good jobs, own two cars, have all the latest gadgets like expensive bikes and sporting equipment, take an annual holiday overseas and domestic holidays throughout the year, and live in a big house in a well-to-do area.
Is it socially acceptable to ask for money publicly in these circumstances?

Eleanor says: I’ll never forget someone posting their household expenses as proof it’s hard to get by on two six-figure incomes. By the time they’d paid for holidays, two cars, private school fees, insurance, extracurriculars, the mortgage and savings, there was nothing left!

They really did think this was proof they weren’t well-off. I suppose in some sense they’re right. Once you use your money to secure your financial future and have a high quality of life, you don’t have a Scrooge McDuck pile left over.
points: Your friends may have had good intentions when making this ask, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith.
But that needn’t dictate how you feel about it.

articles.title: Who needs sleep when you can scroll through home makeover videos instead | Bim Adewunmi
articles.summary: I’m not talking about frenetic whole-house renovations and stripping wallpaper but the slow, thoughtful design tweaks that are perfect for bedtime viewing. I have been doing more than my fair share of revenge bedtime procrastination.
body: I am drawn more and more to the slower projects. People who take years to redo their entire house, and then walk me through each and every design decision. This is what our parents and grandparents did, no? The homes so many of us grew up in were not subject to annual refreshing – who had the time or will to strip all that wallpaper? Not my mum! And we were no poorer for it.

One of my faves is Medina Grillo. She and her family were long-term renters until they recently bought their own home, and I adore how she makes room for trial and error. Her design choices always charm me (I’ve copied her idea of turning dish racks into book and vinyl shelving), and she is so calm and chill.

I also follow Anna Stephens on TikTok. She has a series called “three tweaks per week”, in which she undertakes three little projects and slowly shifts the vibe of her home. It has been almost a year of the videos, and I’m not sick of them yet. It’s such a simple, no-pressure idea. An ideal bedtime scroll destination.
points: I’m not talking about frenetic whole-house renovations and stripping wallpaper but the slow, thoughtful design tweaks that are perfect for bedtime viewing.

articles.title: ‘I wanted to create the female version of a man’s suit’: how Roland Mouret’s Galaxy dress took over the world
articles.summary: One the most famous dresses of this century, it was worn by royalty and A-list celebrities in the noughties. Its latest fans are Maga women. Here, the designer, and former mentor to Victoria Beckham, reveals the story behind it.
body: The story of one of the most photographed and ripped-off dresses of the last 50 years came together with a simple zip. It was 1998; the designer Roland Mouret had shown his first collection at London fashion week and was looking for a way to produce good clothes at speed. He connected with a small British atelier and it was there that some old-school industry wisdom would alter his course: he learned that a longer seam doesn’t actually cost any more than a shorter one.

Despite his brilliantly instinctive approach to design, it was like cracking a code – and steered him towards the dress that would make his name. “My brain was buzzing!” he says. “I hadn’t thought about it before – if you extend a top by 50cm, it becomes a whole outfit. You just need accessories. Focusing on dresses gives you a signature piece at the right price.”

articles.title: Has Substitution Culture Gone Too Far?
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. When Chanita Chayaluk decided to open her restaurant and wine bar Taan, she hoped “to showcase Thai food in Chicago in a different…
body: Guests are increasingly asking for their meals to be customized. These restaurants say it’s gone too far.

Another quirk of operating in Chicago? “We’re still pretty ‘Midwest nice,’” says Chayaluk. “We try to overaccommodate and appease the masses.” In the early days of service, guests made frequent requests for substitutions or accommodations due to preferences and dietary restrictions. “It would slow down service and speed, and that was not just affecting us, but the guest experience in many ways,” she says. With a small kitchen and staff, it was hard to keep up. “It just felt like we were Chipotle.” When a guest asked for green curry mussels “but without the mussels,” it was a turning point.

Chayaluk implemented a limited substitution policy at Taan, stating on Instagram that ingredients like fish sauce and shrimp paste are “the fabric that defines our cuisine,” and therefore, could not be removed from any dishes that include it.
At the same time, restaurants like Taan and New York’s Ha’s Snack Bar —which proudly announces in its Instagram bio that everything contains fish sauce—are standing their ground.
points: Guests are increasingly asking for their meals to be customized.
“We try to overaccommodate and appease the masses.

articles.title: 4 Unconventional Wedding Guest Outfit Ideas for the Non-Traditionalist
articles.summary: Calling all unconventional wedding guests who don’t want to copy-paste their outfit—one writer shares her take on non-traditionalist event dressing.
body: If there’s one thing I’m not, it’s a traditionalist; an ethos that extends from my personal style and interests right into my disinterest in weddings. I never played bridal dress-up as a little girl, instead riding around on a Fisher-Price motorcycle. So while I’m always sincerely happy for my loved ones getting married, I’d be even happier to hear they eloped. Nuptials are possibly my least favorite gathering; the prospect of putting together a note-perfect outfit often only adds to my aversion.

One thing I’ve learned over my years in the guest seat: I may not be able to control my social battery draining by the time the reception rolls around, but I can control what I wear so I still feel like myself. And if you, like me, aren’t interested in throwing on any black suit or floor-length pastel slip dress in the name of easy formality, I’ve put together a few unconventional wedding guest outfit formulas I rely on whenever the occasion calls for it.

articles.title: The Bean Salad WFH Lunch That Tastes Even Better the Next Day
articles.summary: I have been following Violet Witchel, creator of the viral TikTok “dense bean salad” trend, for years. I remember when she graduated from culinary school, something I toy with doing one day.
body: A dense bean salad is a salad you can prep at the beginning of the week with wilt-free ingredients that just gets better as the week goes on. They’re packed with vegetables, beans, protein, cheeses, herbs, homemade dressing, and more. The best part is there are so many potential flavor combinations. My favorite is our Southwest-inspired dense bean salad.

Part of what makes a dense bean salad so good is that you can use what you have on hand. That means finally finding a purpose for that stray can of pinto beans you bought a few months ago or that half of an onion you’ve been trying to use up. But if you happen to plan ahead and decide you want to make a dense bean salad with more than just what you have in the pantry, look no further than this citrusy and vibrant recipe.

articles.title: Kate Middleton’s New Honey Hair Color Is Fall-Ready
articles.summary: Kate, the Princess of Wales, gives “teak brunette” the royal seal of approval. Here's why the glossy, fall-ready shade is trending and what to ask your colorist.
body: The Princess of Wales ’s tumbling hair always turns heads—and fills up Pinterest inspiration boards—but this week, her chosen shade felt decidedly more autumnal against her wardrobe of forest greens and rich blues. While attending a series of engagements over the course of a three-day state visit from the Sultan of Oman, the Princess—who usually visits Chelsea’s Richard Ward salon for her hair color—has unveiled more golden-toned lengths, with subtle waves adding to the glossy finish.

It’s a seasonally appropriate hue that Siobhan Haug, a color specialist and founder of Haug London Haus salon, predicts will come to reign supreme as we head into the colder months. She calls it “teak brunette,” inspired by the tones of teak tree timber in all of its honeyed, golden glory. “On hair, it translates into a medium to dark brown with golden, tawny undertones,” Haug continues, “and it moves from sun-warmed gold to a deeper, softer brown, much like teakwood itself as it matures.”
points: Kate, the Princess of Wales, gives “teak brunette” the royal seal of approval.
